facts: Data: 65 cleaned recordings from 1 members; 2 unseen test recordings with 70 labelled windows.
Sampling rates (accelerometer, median per member): enock 100 Hz; all resampled to 50 Hz.
Easiest activity on the test data: walking (sensitivity 1.00); hardest: jumping (sensitivity 0.44).
Most frequent error: true jumping predicted as standing (8 windows, 50% of jumping).
Adding transitions (Viterbi) vs classifying each window alone: test accuracy 0.757 -> 0.814.
Baum-Welch vs supervised estimate (both Viterbi): test accuracy 0.757 -> 0.814; Baum-Welch converged in 5 iterations.
Expected time in each state before switching: standing 18.4 s, walking 14.1 s, jumping 13.7 s, still 13.3 s.
Most likely switches: still -> standing 0.025; still -> walking 0.025; still -> jumping 0.025.
